outcome: Analgesia or anesthesia management during labor
Obstetrical characteristics (primiparity, preeclampsia, need for magnesium sulphate therapy, chronic hypertension)
cohort: 376 laboring women aged 40 years or above who delivered at a single, tertiary, university affiliated medical center.
finding: While anesthesia management was comparable between parturients aged 40-44 years and those aged ≥45 years, the latter group had a higher risk of postpartum hemorrhage.
